title: Note Placement

illustrates.quote: Do not insert a blank line between a note separation line and a title or heading. (See Sample 16-2: Notes with Headings on page 16-18.)

blocks.text: “I know—that’s what I’m saying—the old stories about the ka’tsina spirit[ref:†] and Yellow Woman can’t mean us.”
blocks.features: Quoted dialogue, with a dagger reference mark after "ka'tsina spirit"; an ellipsis and a short rule line follow it, then a blank gap before the note.

blocks.text: [ref:†]ka'tsina spirit: A mountain spirit of the Laguna Pueblo Indians.
blocks.features: Set below a short horizontal rule at the foot of the print page; "ka'tsina spirit" is bold, the dagger mark precedes it.

braille.notes: The quoted passage (opening/closing quotation marks 8...0, 2-cell indent for the quote) is followed by an ellipsis line (444) then the seven-cell note separation line ("333333, i.e. dots 2-5-6 then six cells of dots 2-5). The footnote itself follows with the dagger mark and its 2-cell runover indent. Line 8 is a line of blank braille cells (U+2800 in the source, recorded here as an empty string) sitting between the note and a second, unrelated dashed rule (a page-layout/continuation rule, ending in the reference code #gbc) that precedes the placeholder word ",text" -- this second rule and placeholder are the guide's own boundary marking for the illustration box, not part of the worked note example proper.

uncertain: Lines 8-10 (the blank-cell line, the long dashed rule ending #gbc, and ",text") sit inside the same source line range as the worked example but read as the guide's own page-boundary graphic rather than further note content; included verbatim since the task requires transcribing the range exactly as given, but flagged here as likely not part of the substantive note-placement illustration itself.
resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.5.1.h per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 12531 is a full 40-cell blank line and line 12532 (the page-change dashed rule ending '#gbc') is exactly 40 characters, with no left padding on this item at all. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
